domain_label: Knowledge-Graph Relation Validation — Logical & Mereological Inconsistency Detection (rule- and reasoner-based catches for antisymmetry, containment cycle, symmetry, transitivity, cardinality, and domain/range-disjointness violations in part_of/related/prereq edges, run deterministically before any LLM)
purpose: The structure-level truth layer of the kgverify specialist: how a relation-validation authority runs DETERMINISTIC integrity and mereological law-checks over the INBDE/USMLE study knowledge graph BEFORE any LLM is invoked — SHACL-style constraint shapes, parthood partial-order laws (transitive, antisymmetric, irreflexive proper-part), relation-algebra checks (symmetry, transitivity closure, cardinality/functionality), and domain/range disjointness — to catch the class of defect a rule can settle with certainty (the observed D1 pituitary↔adrenal part_of inversion), typing each detection by defect class and emitting a RANKED CANDIDATE-DEFECT LIST that is handed to the LLM verification KB (kb2) and never auto-applied. It owns which truth-bearing constraints to run; it defers the schema those constraints check against, and all directionality/DAG/vocabulary governance, to the sibling kgraph.
assumptions: no observed dataset supplied; all base metric scores are heuristic priors and every design call is an ESTIMATE synthesized from the cited literature and the app grounding files

external method claims are grounded in published work and carried inline as [FACT-source: URL]; publisher pages returned 403 to direct fetch (bot-block, not a proxy failure), so citations rest on search-engine summaries that quote those papers and any figure not directly quoted is left unstated rather than invented

clinical/anatomical claims (the D1 pituitary/adrenal mereology) are tagged CLINICAL-FACT and flagged 'to reconfirm against source', consistent with kgverify's own doctrine that it must not assert clinical truth without a citation

the app's ConceptEdge entity with type in {prereq, related, part_of} and a negated flag is the fixed target; this KB specifies which constraints to run over it, not the schema itself, which is owned by the sibling kgraph

this KB is the STRUCTURE-LEVEL TRUTH (deterministic detection) third of the kgverify specialist; content-level truth (LLM claim verification with calibrated confidence) and owner-gated repair/provenance are neighboring KBs this one only hands off to
exclusions: the content-truth verdict on whether a proposition is clinically correct — kb1 flags a candidate defect by defect class; the entailment/contradiction judgment with calibrated confidence is kb2's remit
the repair proposal, owner-gating, and provenance record of any correction (kb3) beyond emitting the typed candidate-defect that a proposal is built from

all graph SCHEMA/STRUCTURE governance — whether an edge is a legal edge, per-type directionality, DAG acyclicity policy, closed-vocabulary changes, node granularity, endpoint existence, hub detection (owned by the sibling kgraph) beyond consuming that schema as the constraint target
the visual rendering of a flagged edge or a negation (owned by viz) and the mastery/scheduling math (owned by learner/sched)
building the SHACL engine, the OWL reasoner, or the pipeline code in the app (owned by app engineering/extint) beyond specifying which constraints and laws such code must run and in what order

glossary.definition: The kgverify/kgraph split: kgverify owns whether an (A,relation,B) proposition is clinically/anatomically CORRECT (and if not, what it should become); kgraph owns whether the edge is WELL-FORMED (typed, acyclic, non-dangling, closed-vocabulary, provenance-labeled). kgraph.boundaries reserves the subject-matter truth of any specific concept to a domain expert or the cited source — kgverify is that authority.

The W3C-standard declarative Shapes Constraint Language that validates a graph against shapes/rules and reports violations, with cardinality, class-membership, and property-pair equality/disjointness as core constraint types [UNVERIFIED-SOURCE: https://arxiv.org/pdf/2112.01441 ; https://www.w3.org/TR/shacl/]; kgverify specifies which truth-bearing constraints to run, kgraph owns the schema they check against.

Parthood is a partial order — transitive, antisymmetric, and (for proper parthood) irreflexive/asymmetric [FACT-source: https://www.w3.org/wiki/PartWhole ; https://plato.stanford.edu/archives/fall2004/entries/mereology/ ; https://eng.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Computer_Science/Book:_An_Introduction_to_Ontology_Engineering_(Keet)/07:_Top-Down_Ontology_Development/7.03:_Part-Whole_Relations]. D1 (mutual part_of) violates antisymmetry and closes a containment cycle.

The deterministic catch for the observed defect: pituitary part_of adrenal cortex AND adrenal cortex part_of pituitary asserts A part_of B and B part_of A, which antisymmetric proper-parthood forbids; caught by a rule with certainty, no LLM required.

Adrenal cortex and medulla are SIBLINGS — both part_of the adrenal gland — so cortex is not part_of medulla; and the pituitary (sella turcica) and adrenal glands (retroperitoneal) are DISTINCT organs, so neither is part_of the other; the real pituitary↔adrenal link is the functional HPA axis (pituitary ACTH stimulates adrenal cortex), a related/causal edge not part_of [CLINICAL-FACT, standard endocrine anatomy — to reconfirm against source].

A constraint that flags a semantic type error when a relation's asserted endpoints belong to disjoint classes — 'a person cannot be the sibling of a building… resulting in logical inconsistency' [UNVERIFIED-SOURCE: https://arxiv.org/html/2502.19023v1]; the analog here flags an organ part_of a hormone.

A data-dependent inconsistency in a relation's algebraic character — symmetry (a related asserted one-way), transitivity closure, and qualified cardinality / (inverse) functionality / (a)symmetricity / irreflexivity [UNVERIFIED-SOURCE: https://arxiv.org/html/2502.19023v1].

Inconsistencies are surfaced after transitive closure using OWL 2 RL/RDF rules and DL reasoners (HermiT, Pellet, FaCT++) that assert asymmetric/disjoint/different-from axioms [UNVERIFIED-SOURCE: https://arxiv.org/html/2502.19023v1 ; https://www.w3.org/TR/prov-o/]; kgverify treats reasoner output as candidate defects, not verdicts.

The discipline of running rule/reasoner checks before any LLM: a law violation (D1) is caught with certainty, cheaper and calibration-free, so only content truth (D2) needs the LLM — mirroring the inconsistency-handling split of detect / fix / inconsistency-tolerant reasoning [UNVERIFIED-SOURCE: https://arxiv.org/html/2502.19023v1].

The output contract: each detection carries a defect-class label (antisymmetry / cycle / cardinality / disjointness / thin-link) so the downstream proposal is typed and auditable; the layer emits a RANKED list of candidate defects handed to kb2, never an auto-edit.

A low-degree node (e.g. heart linking only to atria and aortic arch) flagged as a candidate-missing-edge signal — a completion/recall gap, NOT an inconsistency; the truth of any proposed new edge is handed to kb2, and edges are never invented to fill gaps [UNVERIFIED-SOURCE: https://arxiv.org/html/2502.19023v1 forbids inventing links].

nodes.definition: Order the pipeline deterministic-first. A law violation (D1) is caught by a rule with certainty; only CONTENT truth (D2) needs an LLM. Running rules first is cheaper and calibration-free, and it isolates the class of defect the way inconsistency-handling is split into detect / fix / inconsistency-tolerant reasoning [UNVERIFIED-SOURCE: https://arxiv.org/html/2502.19023v1]. This keeps the expensive, overconfidence-prone LLM off the cases a rule already decides.

nodes.definition: Encode the parthood laws that make part_of checkable. Parthood is a partial order — transitive, antisymmetric, and (for proper parthood) irreflexive/asymmetric [FACT-source: https://www.w3.org/wiki/PartWhole ; https://eng.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Computer_Science/Book:_An_Introduction_to_Ontology_Engineering_(Keet)/07:_Top-Down_Ontology_Development/7.03:_Part-Whole_Relations ; https://plato.stanford.edu/archives/fall2004/entries/mereology/]. From these three laws the D1 defect falls out deterministically: mutual part_of (A part_of B and B part_of A) violates ANTISYMMETRY, and the same pair closes a CYCLE in the containment DAG — a catch requiring no LLM. Transitivity is the positive counterpart: part_of should entail an ancestor edge, and a transitive closure that contradicts an asserted edge is itself a violation. These laws are the mereological core of the constraint set.

nodes.definition: Check each relation type against its algebra. Inconsistencies depend on actual data values and include qualified cardinality, (inverse) functionality, (a)symmetricity and irreflexivity [UNVERIFIED-SOURCE: https://arxiv.org/html/2502.19023v1]. Concretely: symmetry — a related asserted one-way when related is symmetric; transitivity closure — a part_of that should entail an ancestor edge and does not, or a closure that contradicts an asserted edge; cardinality/functionality — a relation that should hold at most once holding many times. workflow.gate: D1 is processed detect-type-rank-handoff with a citation-pending retype, never a delete

workflow.action: Commit the deterministic-detection verdict and defer structure
workflow.description: Commit the constraint+reasoner layer, its candidate-defect output, and the kgraph/viz/learner deferrals
workflow.gate: the committed layer types and ranks candidates, never auto-edits, and defers structure to kgraph

priority_rationale: The committed detection verdict and the antisymmetry/mereology catches lead because they are the certain, high-value core that settles the observed D1 defect; the candidate-not-verdict discipline, the typed-ranked labeling and the D1 worked example come next because they turn a catch into an auditable hand-off rather than a delete; the truth-vs-structure split, the algebra checks, the deterministic-first ordering, the scope fence and the ConceptEdge mapping form the governing and executable layer; and the constraint model, containment-cycle face, D1 anatomy, reasoner closure, thin-link signal, negation hook and the problem frame complete the layer, ordered last because they elaborate or ground the core rather than deciding it.

dominance_rules.rule: Deterministic law-checks dominate the LLM for rule-decidable defects
dominance_rules.rationale: a law violation is certain, cheap and calibration-free, so paying for a model call is waste and risk
dominance_rules.trigger: a defect is expressible as an integrity/mereology/algebra constraint
dominance_rules.action: catch it with the rule/reasoner and never route it to the LLM

dominance_rules.rationale: a mechanical flag names an inconsistency, not which edge is false
dominance_rules.trigger: a rule or reasoner flags an edge as inconsistent
dominance_rules.action: emit a typed candidate and hand the which-is-false verdict to kb2, never auto-delete

dominance_rules.rationale: inventing an edge to raise degree corrupts the graph with false authority
dominance_rules.action: emit a candidate-missing-edge signal and require kb2 to verify any new edge with a citation

dominance_rules.rule: kgraph's structural ownership dominates kgverify's detection when a repair edits schema
dominance_rules.rationale: kgverify owns truth, not the acyclicity/vocabulary/typing of the graph
dominance_rules.trigger: a detected defect's repair would change schema or break a DAG
dominance_rules.action: hand off to kgraph for the legal structural change; kgverify only states the semantic need

dominance_rules.rule: Transitive closure dominates a shallow one-hop scan
dominance_rules.rationale: a laundered inversion behind a chain is invisible to direct-edge checks
dominance_rules.trigger: antisymmetry/disjointness could hide behind a multi-hop path
dominance_rules.action: run the checks over the closure, not just direct edges

dominance_rules.rule: A required citation dominates an asserted clinical claim
dominance_rules.rationale: kgverify must not assert clinical truth without a source
dominance_rules.trigger: a defect's repair rests on an anatomical/clinical claim
dominance_rules.action: tag it CLINICAL-FACT-to-reconfirm and require kb2 to cite a source before it is asserted

dominance_rules.rule: Negation-as-fix dominates delete-as-fix when the truth is a negation
dominance_rules.rationale: a delete erases information a negated edge would preserve
dominance_rules.trigger: a defect's true form is 'A does NOT relate to B'
dominance_rules.action: flag it negation-shaped and hand the negation truth to kb2 rather than proposing a delete

dominance_rules.rule: Mechanical ranking is provisional; clinical severity dominates at kb2
dominance_rules.rationale: rule certainty can bury a clinically dangerous defect
dominance_rules.action: let kb2 re-rank by clinical severity once truth is judged

anti_rework_rules.rule: Fix the truth-vs-structure boundary before writing any check
anti_rework_rules.prevents: kgverify and kgraph both claiming or both disowning a defect and reworking the split later

anti_rework_rules.rule: Run deterministic law-checks before invoking any LLM
anti_rework_rules.prevents: paying model cost and calibration risk on defects a rule settles with certainty

anti_rework_rules.rule: Ground part_of checks in the partial-order laws with citations up front
anti_rework_rules.prevents: vague 'looks inverted' flags that cannot be defended or audited

anti_rework_rules.rule: Treat every rule/reasoner output as a candidate, never a verdict
anti_rework_rules.prevents: deleting a true edge because it conflicts with a false one

anti_rework_rules.rule: Type and rank every detection by defect class from the first pass
anti_rework_rules.prevents: an untyped flag that kb3 cannot map to the right repair operation

anti_rework_rules.rule: Forbid gap-filling by fabrication when handling thin nodes
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a graph populated with plausible-but-uncited edges that must later be swept

anti_rework_rules.rule: Defer schema/DAG/vocabulary repairs to kgraph from the start
anti_rework_rules.prevents: kgverify editing structure it does not own and colliding with kgraph

anti_rework_rules.rule: Tag every clinical claim CLINICAL-FACT-to-reconfirm pending a kb2 citation
anti_rework_rules.prevents: asserting an anatomical repair as settled fact without a source

iteration_protocol.trigger: kgraph publishes or revises the ConceptEdge schema or a relation's algebra
iteration_protocol.action: re-sync the check-to-field mapping and treat the new schema as the single source of truth

iteration_protocol.trigger: a new class of source defect is observed in the live graph
iteration_protocol.action: add a typed constraint/check and a defect-class label for it
activate the domain/range disjointness check that was inactive-pending-typing

iteration_protocol.trigger: the app's reasoner/library is confirmed by recon
iteration_protocol.action: replace the UNKNOWN reasoner class with the confirmed engine and its verified axioms

iteration_protocol.trigger: a real negated edge appears in the source
iteration_protocol.action: exercise the negation hook on real data instead of the synthetic fixture

iteration_protocol.trigger: kb2 re-ranks a defect by clinical severity against the mechanical rank
iteration_protocol.action: record the clinical re-rank as the authoritative priority for that defect

iteration_protocol.trigger: a part-whole flavour mismatch is repeatedly suspected
iteration_protocol.action: flag a possible governed part_of refinement to kgraph rather than loosening the law

required_checks: all edge ids unique EDGE_XXX format
all from/to in edges reference valid node ids
all competency_question_refs resolve to valid CQ ids
all evidence_refs resolve to valid source_registry ids
all priority_order entries are valid node ids with no duplicates
high_risk_nodes (risk_if_wrong>=0.80) have non-empty acceptance_tests and human_review_required=true
conflict edges have signed_tension<0 and resolution_rule present
observed_impact=0.0 for all nodes (no observed data)
18-21 nodes, 34-40 edges, 8-9 conflict_axes, 10-11 edge_cases, 10-12 workflow steps
post_formula_checks: all derived fields non-zero after compute run

test_cases.input_summary: smallest meaningful instance in this domain

evaluation_suite.regression_policy: re-run evaluation suite after any node addition or formula change
